sections.overview: The Varied Thrush is a Turdidae songbird of the Pacific Northwest, breeding in wet mature forests and wintering farther south.
sections.identification: The male has a slate head and breast band, orange breast and flanks, and a bold orange eyebrow; females are duller.
sections.habitat: It breeds in shaded, humid conifer forests and uses parks, gardens and riparian woods in winter.
sections.diet: It gleans insects and other arthropods from leaf litter in summer, then relies more on berries, fruit and acorns in winter.
sections.behavior: It forages on the ground, and males sing to establish territories before females arrive on the breeding grounds.
sections.reproduction: The female builds a cup nest in the forest understory; Cornell reports one or two broods and about 12 days of incubation.
sections.ecology: The European Robin in the existing robin profile belongs to Muscicapidae, not the thrush family Turdidae.
sections.conservation: Canada lists the species as globally Least Concern in 2018, while its national population has declined moderately since about 1970.
